data.text/markdown:
Movers: who moves this afternoon, and which way?

At 13:30 every day, for each stock: will it move by the end of the horizon (15:30), up or down, by at least THETA percent? One TSMixer learns many stocks at once, reads the morning, and answers with three probabilities: down / flat / up. This notebook replaces the end-correlation score of the other TSMixer notebooks:
  • every stock-day counts once: the outcome is a class, so a 5% move weighs exactly as much as a 1% move, and "flat, and it was flat" is a right answer
  • the outcome is in percent, not in the stock's own typical moves, so a move is a move you could trade
  • what is scored is the CALL: with your cash and the size of a position the book holds K positions, so each day the model calls its K likeliest movers, each long or short. Every call is one vote
  • two rules need no model: random picks, and the K stocks with the biggest average move over the last 20 days. The second one is the hurdle: knowing which stocks are active is cheap and already triples the hit rate. The model has to know something on top of it
  • the stocks are an active set: those with 1-minute bars since 2025-01-01 that move most in this window on the TRAIN days (VALIDATION and TEST are never used to pick them)

Settings

The next cell holds every setting, in six blocks. Edit a value and everything below re-runs.
  1. The question: when the prediction is made, how far ahead it looks, what counts as a move
  2. The book: cash and the size of a position, which give the number of calls per day
  3. The stocks and the data: how many stocks, and three consecutive date ranges TRAIN → VALIDATION → TEST (Table 2 shows the exact days)
  4. The inputs: each one True (read), False (not read) or "search" (the optimizer decides, trial by trial); the stock's own path is always read
  5. What the optimizer searches: the history length and TSMixer's knobs (Table 5)
  6. Training: how many passes, when to stop; how many trials

The stocks

The screen looks at every stock with 1-minute bars since UNIVERSE_FROM, on the TRAIN days only: the share of days it moved at least THETA between the decision and the horizon's end, its typical move, price, and the dollars traded in that window. Stocks with gaps or under $1 million traded in the window are dropped; the most active UNIVERSE_N stay (Table 1). The first run takes about a minute; the result is saved in var/movers/.

data.text/markdown:
The data and the split

The 1-minute bars of every stock from TRAIN's first day to TEST's last, and every input built from them (tsmixer_lab.build, the same inputs as the other TSMixer notebooks). Table 2 shows the days:
  • history only: the first 10 sessions, read for the typical sizes, never learned
  • TRAIN: the model learns; its last 10 days are held out to stop the training
  • VALIDATION: every trial is scored here; TEST: read once, at the very end
Table 3 counts the classes: how many stock-days went down, stayed flat, went up. A model that always says "flat" is right on the biggest class, which is why only the calls count.

data.text/markdown:
The hurdle: what needs no model

On each day the two rules call K stocks with a random side. A pick is right when the stock moved at least THETA the called way, which a random side gets half of the time it moved at all. Table 4 is the bar every model has to clear, on TRAIN and on VALIDATION:
  • random picks: any K stocks of the day
  • activity picks: the K stocks with the biggest average move over the last 20 days. No model, no training. This is the rule to beat: a model that only learned which stocks are active will tie it, and only knowing something about today or the direction beats it

data.text/markdown:
The study

Table 5 lists the knobs the optimizer searches. A trial draws them, trains one TSMixer on every stock's TRAIN days (the loss is the cross-entropy of the three classes, every stock-day weighing the same; only flat_weight can turn the flat class down), stops on the 10 held-out days, and calls K stocks a day on VALIDATION. The trial's score is the z of its excess over the activity rule: per day, the share of its calls that are right minus what the activity picks with a random side would get, averaged over days, divided by its standard error over days. It is 0 when the model knows what the activity rule knows and nothing more; above 0, the model adds something. The best of many trials is partly luck: the line above Table 6 gives the z the best of this many trials reaches by chance alone (2.5% of the time).

data.text/markdown:
TEST: read once

The best trial is trained again on TRAIN and VALIDATION (its held-out days are the last ones of VALIDATION) with the same settings and seed, and calls the TEST days. Press once: whatever it says, the study must not be tuned on it afterwards. If the best trial was within luck on VALIDATION, TEST is the only honest look at whether it knows anything.
Press the button to read TEST (once).
